scope: same two preselected SWE-bench train failures; opt-in dual-checkout assertion experiment

baseline_integrity.probe_mounts: read-only, offline, same image and platform as candidate
baseline_integrity.checks: HEAD and git status including untracked and ignored files before and after each pair

cases.observation: A probe created after editing got a genuine base-fail/current-pass result. The narrow Not Supplied fallback and an invalid-encoding compatibility check passed, but all three official target tests failed.

The first pair correctly rejected original-fail/current-fail. Later deduplication in the internal linter produced red-green evidence and passed official grading, but the base-checkout public test expected duplicate violations. That local failure persisted, a test-edit attempt was blocked, and the Agent exhausted 30 turns without full verification. The local/official test-oracle mismatch needs a separate audit before any gate change.

strict_sft_export.note: Exporter reports the first failing gate only; pydicom is also officially unresolved. The existing eight-sample accepted corpus was not changed.

conclusion: Dual checkouts remove the requirement to run a probe before editing while preserving an auditable same-code counterfactual. They do not solve narrow assertion coverage, invalid JSON, or conflicts between base-checkout tests and official grading. No new strict training sample was accepted.
limitations: One stochastic sample per task and an unpinned provider revision do not establish causal improvement over prior variants.
A passing pair proves only the model-written assertion, not complete issue resolution.
The model never received official test patches, target test identities, or gold patches; report analysis was post-hoc.
Changed initial prompts cannot form exact-prompt preference pairs with older trajectories.
No held-out rollout, GPU job, SFT, LoRA, or RL training was performed.
